query: What are the two evaluation splits used in the political ideology bias paper, and how do they differ?
reference_answer: The Media-based Split tests on 1,200 articles from 12 news media not seen during training (excluding the remaining 5,470 articles from those media). The Random Split uses the same test set but adds those excluded 5,470 articles back into the training/validation pool via stratified random sampling, so training and evaluation sources overlap.
key_facts: media-based split: test set from 12 media unseen during training

query: What are the two de-biasing techniques proposed in the political ideology bias paper to prevent models from learning the news source instead of political ideology?
reference_answer: Adversarial Adaptation (AA), which adds a media classifier with a gradient reversal layer so the encoder's representation becomes invariant to the source medium, and Triplet Loss Pre-training (TLP), which pre-trains the encoder so articles with the same ideology from different media are pulled closer together than same-media articles with different ideology.
key_facts: Adversarial Adaptation (AA) uses a media classifier with gradient reversal
Triplet Loss Pre-training (TLP) pre-trains the encoder on anchor/positive/negative triplets
both aim to stop the model from modeling the source medium instead of ideology

query: According to the political ideology bias paper's de-biasing results (Table 5), how much did Triplet Loss Pre-training (TLP) improve performance over the baseline on the media-based split?

query: In the Political DEBATE paper's COVID-19 threat-minimization few-shot experiment, how did the DEBATE large model's performance at 10 and 25 training samples compare to the supervised Electra classifier trained by Block Jr. et al.?

query: How do the entailment/NLI foundation models differ between the zero-shot text classification paper and the Political DEBATE paper?
reference_answer: The zero-shot classification paper uses BERT as its entailment model, trained on three general-purpose entailment datasets: MNLI, GLUE RTE, and FEVER. The Political DEBATE paper instead starts from DeBERTa V3 base/large models already fine-tuned for general NLI (on five NLI datasets and 28 other classification datasets) by Laurer et al., and further trains them on the domain-specific PolNLI dataset for political text.
key_facts: zero-shot paper uses BERT trained on MNLI, GLUE RTE, FEVER
Political DEBATE uses DeBERTa V3 models pre-trained for general NLI by Laurer et al.
Political DEBATE further trains on the domain-specific PolNLI dataset

query: Compare how the news-article political ideology paper, the political leaning/politicalness paper, and the Political DEBATE paper each approach political-leaning classification.
reference_answer: The news-article ideology paper trains supervised LSTM and BERT classifiers directly on labeled left/center/right articles. The political leaning/politicalness paper instead evaluates zero-shot NLI classifiers, including Political DEBATE, using the hypothesis "This text supports {left | center | right} political leaning." The Political DEBATE paper is the source of that underlying model, a DeBERTa-based NLI classifier trained on the PolNLI dataset for zero/few-shot political text classification rather than supervised training on a single labeled dataset.
key_facts: news-article ideology paper trains supervised LSTM/BERT classifiers
political leaning paper uses zero-shot NLI hypothesis 'This text supports {left|center|right} political leaning'
Political DEBATE paper introduces the underlying DeBERTa-based NLI model trained on PolNLI
